answer: Each identity must lock a refundable work-bond that only unlocks after several independently graded epochs. An attacker who wants to wander through dozens of shell accounts pays that bond on every mint, so farm cost scales linearly with heads, not with names. A cheap sparrow-tier sampler checks coherence first; a rarer falcon juror then re-grades a random subset and can slash the bond if the two disagree on planted junk. The attacker therefore loses both capital and future seats, which is more expensive than inventing extra aliases.
